https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: Fiona Simpson, the Queensland minister for women, says claims that she deems the word ‘gender’ to be ‘on the nose’ and ‘loaded’ are utterly false. Photograph: Darren England/AAP View image in fullscreen Fiona Simpson, the Queensland minister for women, says claims that she deems the word ‘gender’ to be ‘on the nose’ and ‘loaded’ are utterly false. Photograph: Darren England/AAP Queensland politics Mentions of ‘gender’ scrubbed from Queensland Office for Women website amid alleged effort to ‘dewokify’ Comparisons of live and archived pages show more than 20 mentions have been removed, including in reference to the gender pay gap Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Joe Hinchliffe Tue 4 Aug 2026 11.00 EDT Last modified on Tue 4 Aug 2026 11.01 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google References to “gender equality” have been removed from the Queensland Office for Women’s website amid claims by former staffers that the Liberal National party government wants to “dewokify” the public service. Guardian Australia has seen an email from a manager, sent in January, tasking staff with scanning the website for the word “gender” so that it could be “reframed”. Web archives from that month show six prominently displayed references to “gender equality” or “gender equal” were removed from the Office for Women’s “About” page , including from its mission statement that had said: “We’re working towards a gender equal Queensland.” A new Queensland bill aims to ‘streamline’ major projects. Matt and Caitlin fear it could hand their farm to developers Read more “A gender equal Queensland” previously appeared as the first tab on the page’s toolbar. The phrase also appeared in the first sentence of text and was used in the first dot point describing the office’s role. As of Tuesday, no mention of “gender” appears on that page. Across the website, comparisons of archived and live pages show more than 20 mentions of “gender” were removed, including in reference to the gender pay gap. Some mentions of “gender equality” remain, including on the homepage. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email Former department staff said they had received internal requests to have the term “gender” scrubbed from much of the office’s online portal, claiming they were told that the minister for women, Fiona Simpson, deemed the word to be “on the nose” and “loaded”. In a statement to the Guardian, Simpson said this was “utterly false”. “The website was recently updated for the launch of Queensland’s first Women’s Economic Security Strategy – which was designed by Queensland women, for Queensland women,” Simpson said. “While some are worried about words on websites, the Crisafulli government is focused on backing Queensland women.” The former department staffers, who asked to remain anonymous, alleged their managers relayed to them that the word “gender” should be obscured as it “made the LNP think of the LGBTIQA+ community” and they needed to “dewokify”. One ex-employee said they pushed back against the requests. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks Preview latest after newsletter promotion “I was like: ‘Sorry I can’t think of an alternative for gender,’” they said. “Because, I’m sorry, but black and white, on paper, in this instance, gender is men and women and the pay gap that women are experiencing and have been experienced. “Why are we making this a queer issue?” During parliamentary estimates last week, the shadow minister for women, Shannon Fentiman, asked the department of women’s director general, Natalie Wilde, why references to phrases like “gender equality” were removed from the website. Wilde replied that her portfolio “continues routinely to review and update its web presence to improve the user experience for all Queenslanders”. “Editorial changes to web copy are something that is very operational,” Wilde said. “It is approved and managed through my strategic communication unit and is done very much at a business level.” As well as removing many instances of the word “gender”, the recent revamp of the Office for Women’s website also included changing its banner colour from purple to blue and stamping it with the slogan “delivering for Queensland” – both of which are associated with the LNP brand. The Centre for Public Integrity director, Geoffrey Watson SC, has previously criticised such use of the logo across government departments and agencies as politicising the public service. https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: Rescuers seaarch for survivors in the rubble of a collapsed building in Pereira, Colombia, on Monday. Photograph: Jaime Saldarriaga/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Rescuers seaarch for survivors in the rubble of a collapsed building in Pereira, Colombia, on Monday. Photograph: Jaime Saldarriaga/AFP/Getty Images First Thing newsletter US news First Thing: Colombia reels after major earthquake kills at least 130 Buildings collapse and more than 470 people hurt in 7.4-magnitude quake. Plus, in such a vast universe why is there no sign of aliens? Martin Belam Tue 11 Aug 2026 08.11 EDT Last modified on Tue 11 Aug 2026 08.15 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Good morning. More than 130 people died after a powerful earthquake struck western Colombia , collapsing and severely damaging scores of buildings in main cities, including Cali and Pereira. The US and Colombian geological surveys reported that a 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck at 7.34am local time on Monday, with its epicentre in the western department of Chocó. It was felt in neighbouring Venezuela, still reeling from a deadly double earthquake on 24 June. The quake killed at least 132 people and more than 570 were injured as of Monday afternoon, according to the Colombian Association of Capital Cities, which coordinates cities across the country. How has the government responded ? In a national address, Colombia’s president, Abelardo de la Espriella, said: “The ⁠national government has all of its capabilities deployed to protect lives, assist affected communities and deliver aid wherever it is ​needed. The first priority is rescuing the people trapped under the rubble. Colombia has a president whose heart aches for his people and who will do everything in his power to help them in the most difficult moments.” Trump reportedly hid in catering container to board secret flight from Turkey amid Iran threat View image in fullscreen A catering truck is parked next to Air Force One before Donald Trump was due to leaves the Nato summit in Ankara on 8 July. Photograph: Alex Brandon/AP Donald Trump left Turkey on a secret military flight to Britain last month when the White House said he was flying aboard ⁠Air Force One, in an extraordinary ruse – prompted by an Iranian assassination threat – that involved hiding the president in an airport catering container , according to reports. The operation took place when Trump was in Ankara for a Nato summit with world leaders, the Washington Post reported. The president reportedly boarded the old Air Force One jumbo jet in view of television cameras, and was secretly shuttled minutes later to a smaller plane via an airport catering truck, typically used to load meals and other supplies preflight, a US official told the Post. A US official told the Post that a credible threat to Trump involving Iran set the “deception operation” in motion. A similar operation took place in 2000, when Bill Clinton used an unmarked executive jet to fly into Pakistan while sending his formal Air Force One as a decoy. The Guardian has contacted the White House and the US defense department for comment. Trump signs order attempting to override CDC vaccine schedule and break up MMR shots View image in fullscreen President Donald Trump holds a signed executive order about vaccines as Robert F Kennedy looks on. Photograph: Jacquelyn Martin/AP Donald Trump has signed an executive order with plans for sweeping changes to the childhood vaccination schedule that attempts to override the authority of the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The CDC is the federal agency tasked with recommending vaccines, not the White House. Both Trump and Robert F Kennedy, the health secretary, made repeated mentions of autism throughout the signing, emphasizing a scientifically unproven link between vaccines and the condition. Dozens of studies show no link between the two. What does the order seek to change? The order would require that the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine be broken into three separate shots, once it becomes available in the US. It would recommend that all shots be given at separate medical visits, a frequent point Trump has made despite the safety, ease and lower costs of giving vaccines together. Bernie Sanders calls on Silicon Valley to ‘pause AI development’ in interest of humanity View image in fullscreen Bernie Sanders says AI may ‘lead to new bioweapons’. Photograph: John Oliva/Caller-Times/USA Today Network/Reuters Connect Senator Bernie Sanders has called on Meta, OpenAI and Anthropic executives to halt their development of artificial intelligence , saying the US Senate would implement regulation if the companies continued deploying AI at their current pace. Sanders said the capabilities of these AI models had reached a critical risk threshold. The Vermont senator cited recent reports that AI was used to develop new viruses , warning if this technology fell into the “wrong hands” it might “lead to new bioweapons that result in the deaths of tens of millions of people”. All three companies have disclosed their models hacked other companies’ servers, a sign that the firms have lost control, Sanders said. What has Mark Zuckerberg said about AI this week? Sanders’s call comes as the Meta CEO, Mark Zuckerberg, presented a utopian vision of AI in a 6,000-word essay amid Silicon Valley debate over government regulation. Central to Zuckerberg’s post was an argument for free-to-download, open-weight AI models – such as the kind Meta develops – and a lack of government regulation. What has a new study suggested the impact of AI might be on carbon output ? AI-driven productivity gains will enable more planet-heating pollution from fossil fuels than they avoid by boosting energy from renewables, a study has found . In other news … View image in fullscreen Todd Blanche is sworn in. Photograph: Brendan Smialowski/AFP/Getty Images Todd Blanche, Donald Trump’s former personal lawyer, has been sworn in as US attorney general after the Senate voted narrowly in favor of his confirmation. A judge has temporarily blocked Zohran Mamdani’s pied-à-terre tax , which would place a surcharge on second homes in New York City. Republicans have named Jennifer Balkcom as the candidate to replace Chuck Edwards in North Carolina’s 11th congressional district after he had stepped away from the contest owing to a sexual harassment investigation. Nevada authorities are investigating dozens of mysterious tree poisonings in Lake Tahoe since 2022 that appear linked. Jackie, the beloved bald eagle at California’s Big Bear Lake whose livestream was followed by millions of viewers, has died . She was 14. Stat of the day: Trump’s media company, which also owns Truth Social, reports $238m loss View image in fullscreen Photograph: John Minchillo/AP Trump Media & Technology on Monday reported $238m of losses in the three months through June as the company branched into new ventures, including crypto, and began selling a new Truth API service charging $60,000-$100,000 a month for early access to potentially market-moving posts by the US president. Culture Pick: Cults, heists and big cats: TV’s 25 best ever true-crime shows View image in fullscreen Nxivm leader Keith Raniere in a court sketch. Photograph: Jane Rosenberg/Reuters This list from Michael Hogan should give you more than a few ideas for something to binge next time you get that true-crime itch. Don’t miss this: ‘Shoved the tube so hard it tore my nose’: Kurdish film-maker recounts ‘inhumane’ ICE force-feeding View image in fullscreen The Kurdish film-maker Gabar Choli. Photograph: Cole Burston/The Guardian Gabar Choli, a film-maker and activist for an independent Kurdistan, has spoken out for the first time, talking exclusively to the Guardian , about his ordeal in the US. He said being force-fed by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) “broke” him. Or this: How America is losing its mall ice rinks View image in fullscreen An ice rink in Portland. Photograph: Michael Hanson/the Washington Post/Getty Images The Portland rink where Tonya Harding first skated was an affordable community institution for six decades. Its closure echoes the disappearance of mall ice across the US. Talia Barrington investigates . Climate check: July was hottest month ever recorded in US as heatwaves scorched country View image in fullscreen A family cool off in a fountain in Washington DC. Photograph: Kevin Lamarque/Reuters Last month’s average temperature was 3.3F (1.8C) higher than the 20th-century average for the contiguous US as repeated, scorching heatwaves across much of the country helping shatter all previous monthly temperature records . Scientists have made clear the increased heat in the US was being amplified by the human-caused climate crisis. Last Thing: The great silence – why haven’t we found any aliens yet? View image in fullscreen The universe should be full of aliens given its size and age. Photograph: Christopher Thomond/The Guardian I have long been obsessed with space, but one thing has always puzzled me: a universe so vast, how could we possibly be alone? Adam Kirsch has this fascinating read, asking just that question. Given the size and age of the universe, it should be full of species with technology far more advanced than our own. https://www.baltictimes.com/metrosert_ap.text: Estonia Latvia Lithuania Business Analysis Opinions Culture EU Affairs Search Archive Metrosert Appoints New Management Board 2026-08-03 Estonian applied research centre and national metrology institute, Metrosert, has appointed a new management board led by physicist, materials scientist and technology executive Madis Raukas. The three-member board also includes Raul Vahisalu and Monika Isak-Johanson. Madis Raukas , who has taken up the role of Chairman of the Management Board, brings nearly 30 years of international experience in research and development across the United States, Germany and Estonia. Throughout his career, he has contributed to numerous scientific publications and patent applications and has led R&D activities in international technology companies in the fields of materials science, photonics and semiconductor technologies. In recent years, he headed the Applied Research Programme at the Estonian Business and Innovation Agency (EIS) and served as a member of Metrosert’s Supervisory Board since 2023. According to Jana Salm, Chair of Metrosert’s Supervisory Board, Madis Raukas stood out among the candidates thanks to his unique combination of experience as a scientist, technology developer and senior executive. “Madis has a strong understanding of how to translate scientific results into practical applications. He is also deeply familiar with Estonia’s research and innovation ecosystem as well as Metrosert’s activities. His combination of experience, expertise and leadership makes him exceptionally well positioned to lead Metrosert through its next stage of development,” said Salm. According to Madis Raukas, Chairman of Metrosert’s Management Board, Metrosert will focus in the coming years on expanding its applied research capabilities to help Estonian companies identify the most suitable development and testing pathways and bring higher value-added products and technologies to market more quickly. “Our goal is for Metrosert to be the partner companies turn to when they need to transform complex scientific knowledge into practical solutions and bring new ideas to market. The new management board will focus on increasing the impact of applied research while gradually strengthening Metrosert’s long-term economic sustainability,” said Raukas. “I am delighted to begin this work together with Raul Vahisalu and Monika Isak-Johanson, who bring valuable expertise in technology development, international business, quality management and regulatory compliance. Our knowledge and experience complement each other well and provide a strong foundation for achieving Metrosert’s strategic objectives,” he added. Raul Vahisalu is a technology and business development executive with extensive experience in digital identity, cybersecurity, data analytics, telecommunications and dual-use technologies. He has held senior positions at Telia, Guardtime and Global Voice Group and has led international technology development and business operations across Europe, Africa, Asia and the Middle East. Monika Isak-Johanson has extensive experience in developing and managing processes in science- and technology-intensive organisations. Her strengths include scaling business processes, strengthening operational capabilities and commercialising technology-based services. She has held senior leadership roles in pharmaceutical, medical diagnostics and software companies, including GSK, SYNLAB and SoftComply, where she has been responsible for operational transformation, change management, and the development and execution of international growth strategies. Metrosert is Estonia’s state-owned applied research centre and national metrology institute. Its applied research activities focus on five strategic fields: drone technologies, autonomous vehicles, hydrogen technologies, biorefining and health data. Employing approximately 140 leading specialists and researchers, Metrosert supports Estonia’s sustainable economic growth by strengthening collaboration between science and industry. https://www.heraldscotland.com/life_styl.text: Kevin McKenna At Large Castles Environment Heritage History Leisure Travel Walking and outdoors Eilean Donan Castle: Why Scotland’s iconic landmark is worth a vsit By Kevin McKenna Columnist of the Year Share 0 Comments The Eilean Donan castle in the western Highlands of Scotland (Image: Getty) This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. I’d driven past Eilean Donan Castle often, each time reproaching myself for not having stopped to visit. On assignments up the north-west coast towards Skye and beyond, I’d see Scotland’s most enchanting castle emerging round that bend on the A87, on the shores of Loch Duich, at the point where it meets its two sister firths, Long and Alsh. And as I drove slowly past it, wondering if there was enough time for an unplanned shuftie, I’d always hear the sepulchral voice of Virgil Sollozzo in The Godfather : “Ah, make time, Consigliere.” But there had always been a deadline to chase down, made sharper still by the impending challenges of camper vans and tractors. And besides, merely sparing a few minutes for the majesty of Eilean Donan Castle would have seemed sacrilegious, like asking the Queen if she wouldn’t mind awfully hurrying up — if it was all the same to her — because you had a train to catch. I’d first heard of this place from an old history teacher, who would cite it as the ultimate measure by which a location’s beauty could be assessed. “It’s as beautiful as Eilean Donan Castle,” he’d say. Or, if he was dismissing another location’s claim to be so: “We’re not exactly talking Eilean Donan here.” Read more: Memorial commemorating Highland women who fought to save their land unveiled Don't laugh - but this Scottish Labour leadership election actually matters Forget the fancy-dan football. Let's showcase the authentic Scottish experience Shameless Sturgeon rewrites history – but fools no one In my lowland, west-of-Scotland ignorance, I’d heard it as Helen Dornan’s Castle and wondered if it was an aphorism — which he was wont to drop — named for some mythical Irish wanton from the ‘Oul Country. Then, a few years later, I finally saw what he’d been talking about when I went to see Highlander at the cinema. There were those iconic opening scenes, with the 15th-century Clan MacLeod warriors striding out to battle along Eilean Donan’s battlements, each side adorned with the twisting, caged corpses of vanquished foes. Even then, my first thought was that this must have been an extravagant movie set, designed according to the instructions of a Hollywood location director: “Make me a castle that immediately takes you to the Scottish Highlands .” Did a place as heart-achingly grand and gorgeous really exist in Scotland? Why had no one told me about this? And there it remained at the top of my life inventory, alongside the Bernabéu, the San Siro, the Maracanã and the Sistine Chapel, silently chastising me as if to say: “Your time’s running out, sunshine, and you’ve still not been up to see me.” Until last Sunday, when a proper break up the west coast finally gave me some time. Diorama of recreated 1930s kitchen inside Eilean Donan Castle (Image: Getty) I’m assuming many of you will know about the history of Eilean Donan, but bear with me nonetheless. It bears repeating, if only because few others among Scotland’s 2,000 or so castles have featured so prominently in Scotland’s big, life-changing moments. Aye, you can talk about your Edinburgh , your Stirling and your Dunrobin — that stately ancestral home of the pestilential Sutherlands, who brutally evicted thousands of their tenants in the 19th century. None, though, has a setting as naturally pristine as Eilean Donan, where the waters beneath you and the hills above still echo with the deeds — for better and for ill — that bequeathed us this Scotland. The castle is named for St Donan, who lived on this tiny island and helped bring Christianity to the Western Isles near the beginning of the 7th century. The first castle came in the 12th century, constructed by King Alexander II against the Vikings, who had annexed most of the north-west coast and the Hebrides . It became the seat of the Mackenzies — Kenneth, son of Kenneth or, in the old tongue, Coinneach MacCoinneach — who had regained these lands for Alexander III. One of the more eye-catching — or eye-watering — events that took place here occurred in the reign of Robert the Bruce, who always had a soft spot for Eilean Donan. The Bruce had taken shelter here in the early 14th century after defeat at the Battle of Methven had made him persona non grata in the Highlands and an enemy of England’s ruthless Edward Longshanks. On later fighting his way to the throne, Robert showed his own ruthless streak by sending his nephew to impose a sort of martial law. This involved rounding up 50 known local delinquents, decapitating them and displaying their heads on the castle walls as a warning. It’s this event, I think — and fervently hope — that was referenced in those opening scenes in Highlander . Indeed, the clan battle about to be fought by Connor MacLeod and his kinsmen was a brutal feature of those years. I’m less sure about his Spanish pal, Ramirez, and that big fruit-loop, the Kurgan, right enough … Then came the Jacobite Uprising of 1719, when the clans were called out by the exiled King James II to support his doomed claim to the British throne, backed by the Catholic Spanish. And so it was that a ridiculously token Spanish force, comprising 48 men, found itself staring down the mustered cannon of three Royal Navy ships, which proceeded to scatter them before blowing up the castle with its own stores of gunpowder. The English, not surprisingly, still had unresolved trauma with gunpowder from a century earlier, when the Pope’s first team had come agonisingly close to doing in Westminster. So perhaps, understandably, this was their way of laying their demons to rest. The felonies and malfeasances of landowners and aristocrats have long scarred these lands, but credit where it’s due. The scorched pile left by the English navy is what might still be here were it not for Lieutenant John Macrae-Gilstrap, who bought the island in 1911 and set about faithfully reconstructing it with Farquhar Macrae, whose descendants still own it. What we see today is the result of a 20-year endeavour costing about the equivalent of £20m. Courtyard of Eilean Donan Castle at Loch Duich (Image: Getty) So, three cheers to the Lieutenant and the Macraes, and let’s have no more of your infantile mockery of toffs named Farquhar. According to the official castle guide: “The design we see today came to Farquhar MacRae in a dream. The conception was later confirmed to be faithful to the original design when old plans were discovered stored in Edinburgh Castle.” The restoration of Eilean Donan Castle is surely, then, one of the most important cultural and architectural interventions in Scotland’s history. And thank God for it too. If John and Farquhar hadn’t embarked on this sacred undertaking, one of our heritage agencies and the Scottish Government would eventually have reimagined it according to their own cultural ukases and dogma. There would be warnings all over these walls telling visitors that they would encounter real 18th-century guns and cannonballs, and that there would be vivid depictions of unpleasantness and beastliness on their tour. And that, should they be triggered, there would be an on-site counselling service. The old warriors and the kings who employed them would come with newly updated legends beneath their pictures, telling us that, in the interests of inclusive context, some of them might have had dodgy connections to the slave trade. The beautifully rendered imagining of the 18th-century kitchen and living quarters features mannequins of servants and female cooks, along with artistic models of beast and fowl hanging from the walls. This too would not have escaped Scotland’s 21st-century cultural commissars. There would have been a soft-play area for the children, because the heritage community doesn’t think young people are sufficiently intelligent to understand history without lots of goofy smiles and happy endings. Robert the Bruce would be on a loop, depicted as a cartoon character fighting not an English king but the evils of climate change, with a spider telling him about the importance of the environment. Last Sunday, when I rocked up, the castle grounds were absolutely hoaching with tourists, all paying the none-too-shabby entrance fee of £13 per adult — much cheaper for children. I actually walked in and around them for half an hour and counted around a dozen different nationalities. And I swear to God that I didn’t hear another Scottish accent. They were all simply thrilled and enchanted by Eilean Donan Castle, many of them also choosing to hire the headphones that provided recorded commentary in several languages. In the queue for the ticket desk, there were Poles, Japanese and a Bangladeshi family ahead of me. I know this because the lady at the kiosk window took time to ask each visitor if they’d travelled far to be here. “I hear Warsaw’s brilliant,” she told them. She then said they would always be very welcome in Scotland. I felt a little sheepish when I reached her. “I’m from Glasgow,” I said. “Have you been here before?” she asked. “Eh, well, no,” said I. “Well, I can guarantee you that you’ll be back here often,” she said. And she’s absolutely spot-on. You don’t visit Eilean Donan; you experience it and live it. And one visit isn’t nearly enough. Eilean Donan Castle admission: adults, £13; seniors aged 60-plus, £12; children aged five to 15, £5.75 during peak summer (£6.50 outwith this period). Family tickets for two adults and up to three children cost £33.25 in peak season. Free admission for children under five. Tickets are sold on site only. https://business-review.eu/tech/techange.text: TechAngels: Over €1 million in direct investments in H1 2026 In H1 2026, 22% of members made at least one direct investment, compared with approximately 18% in the same period last year. 14% invested in new startups, versus 11% in H1 2025, while participation in follow-on rounds remained broadly stable at approximately 8%. In value terms, follow-on rounds attracted larger volumes of capital, while investments in new startups involved a greater number of members. This suggests that investors are combining the exploration of new opportunities with continued support for companies that have already demonstrated a degree of validation. For the second half of the year, reported intentions for direct investments total €2.18 million, more than twice the amount invested during the first six months. At the same time, 58% of respondents say they intend to continue investing in 2026, provided they identify the right opportunities. This pattern is similar to the one observed in 2025, when investment intentions for H2 significantly exceeded the level of investments made in the first half of the year, suggesting that investment appetite remains present but is increasingly dependent on the quality of opportunities and broader market conditions. “ The first-half data shows an active community that remains highly attentive to the quality of opportunities. Direct investments are slightly higher than in the same period last year, while the intentions reported for the second half indicate that capital is available for founders who can clearly demonstrate the problem they are solving, traction and a credible path to growth. TechAngels aims to contribute to building a strong and consistent deal flow, helping founders become better prepared for fundraising and fostering closer collaboration among members of the community ,” said Ana Maria Andronic, President of TechAngels . Alongside the reported investments, deal flow remained consistent. Between January and June 2026, TechAngels members screened 128 startups and met 35 teams in pitch sessions. The composition of the pipeline shows a strong orientation toward solutions addressing business processes, operations, security, healthcare, education, infrastructure and digital interaction. Read more about Half-year figures 2026: Bosch reaffirms outlook with focus on focus on competitiveness and robustness read more By company type, the largest category consisted of B2B startups focused on enterprise workflow, operational, compliance and security software, accounting for 34.3% of the total. Companies in the health, wellbeing and education space represented 25.7%, while marketplace, community and consumer engagement startups accounted for 20%. A further 20% of the companies analysed operated in hardware, deeptech, infrastructure, dual-use or industrial technologies. An analysis of the problems addressed reveals a similar pattern. 37.1% of startups target business, operational, security or compliance processes that remain manual, fragmented or inefficient. Another 22.9% focus on discovery, engagement, marketplace liquidity, content or community interaction. Solutions addressing physical, technical, industrial, energy or security infrastructure account for 20%, while another 20% focus on individual behaviour, wellbeing, education, habits or personal performance. One particularly strong cross-cutting feature is the prevalence of AI: 68.6% of the startups seen in pitch sessions included AI as a material component of their solution. This significant share confirms that AI is no longer emerging solely as a standalone vertical, but increasingly as a technology layer embedded across products and industries. “ We are seeing more and more projects move beyond general-purpose software products and address complex problems in industries where technology can deliver greater efficiency, control, security or access to data. For investors, this also means more complex evaluation processes and a growing need to draw on highly specific domain expertise ,” added Ana Maria Andronic. During the first half of the year, TechAngels also continued to play a broader facilitating role within the tech ecosystem, beyond its investment activity. The network participated as a partner, speaker or contributor in relevant local and European initiatives, including EBAN Congress 2026, PODIM, CyberSecurity Dialogues, ANIS International Summit, FAST Forum, Work Evolution Summit and Romania Startup Awards. Its involvement in these initiatives focused both on connecting founders with investors and mentors and on strengthening the wider conversation around strategic sectors such as AI, deeptech, cybersecurity, dual-use technologies, aerospace, healthtech and technology infrastructure. In the coming months, TechAngels members will continue to be present in key startup and investment communities in Romania and across the region. Founders looking for funding, feedback or investor connections will be able to meet members of the network at events including How to Web, ScaleUp Fest Budapest, EBAN Summit and MeOut Budapest, where TechAngels will continue to engage with entrepreneurs, investors and partners interested in building technology companies with regional and global potential. TechAngels is Romania’s most experienced community of private investors supporting the growth of technology startups in Romania and across the region. The network brings together more than 130 members, including entrepreneurs and C-level professionals, who invest capital, expertise and time. The aggregated portfolios of TechAngels members include more than 270 startups, while investments made over the past 13 years exceed €46 million. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckx2.text: Image source, Instagram/Finance with Harish Image caption, V Harish ran a hugely popular Instagram handle called "Finance with Harish" By Geeta Pandey ,Â Social affairs editor, India Â and Â Mohan ,Â BBC Tamil Published 7 hours ago A 27-year-old finance influencer's suicide in India has been mired in allegations of cyberbullying and started a conversation around who should give financial advice to investors. V Harish - who ran a hugely popular Instagram account called "Finance with Harish" - was found dead on Tuesday morning at his home near Chennai, capital of the southern state of Tamil Nadu. His suicide came just weeks after his account was disabled by Meta after complaints of irregularities. In a complaint lodged with the police, his father J Vinayagam has alleged that his son took his life because of online harassment by Jason Samuel, a YouTuber and CEO of tech-centric venture studio Zemuria. Police arrested Samuel on Thursday under suspicion of trying to "extort money from Harish" and posting "defamatory videos against him on social media". BBC Tamil has not been able to reach him for comment. Earlier, he denied wrongdoing in a post on X. The case has brought into focus the growing influence of financial content creators in India, where millions of first-time investors increasingly turn to social media for market advice. Account was taken down Harish began posting videos about finance and investing around five years ago, building a substantial online following. Over the years, he published more than 1,500 videos and amassed more than 1.3 million Instagram followers. He described himself as a financial adviser to "millionaires" and "high-net-worth individuals". He often used music, film clips and photos of global political leaders to make dramatic videos while talking about the rise and fall of the share market and prices of gold and silver. The videos, which broke down financial issues in simple terms, became hugely popular as they coincided with a rapid expansion in India's retail investor base, especially since the 2020 Covid-19 pandemic. The country's largest stock exchange, the National Stock Exchange, said earlier this year it now had more than 130 million unique investors registered with it as opposed to under 30 million in 2019. But in September, Meta took down Harish's Instagram page after receiving complaints he was not registered with Indian market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) - which is required under law to be able to offer investment advice or manage client portfolios. A back-up account, which gained over 60,000 followers in a short time, was also subsequently taken down , external following complaints from social media users and others. A few other accounts in his name remain on Instagram, though with much smaller followings - and it's not clear who runs them. According to Harish's friends and family, he recorded a video message before his death in which he said that "five years of hard work has been stolen" from him, news channel NDTV reported , external . The video, which has also been shared widely on social media, shows him speaking in Tamil and then switching to English to say "I'm very sorry" to his parents, sister, friends and followers. Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Meta took down Harish's account after complaints that he was not registered with Sebi, which is required under law to be able to offer investment advice or manage client portfolios. Police complaint Police say Harish's father J Vinayagam has blamed "cyberbullying, defamatory social media posts and repeated blocking of his channels" for his son's suicide and named Jason Samuel in his complaint registered at Kanathur police station near Chennai. Samuel had posted a video on his YouTube channel on 18 October questioning Harish's credentials since he did not have Sebi or Amfi (Association of Mutual Funds in India) registrations. In it, he mentioned that Harish's Instagram account had been disabled following complaints. This, Vinayagam says, triggered severe online harassment and led to pressures that drove his son to take his own life. "We demand that a proper investigation be conducted and legal action be taken against Jason Samuel and his accomplices, who spread defamation on social media and caused mental distress through cyberbullying," his complaint states. A police statement says Vinayagam's complaint was registered under "abetment to suicide" and preliminary investigations found Samuel had a "role in this case". "[Samuel] will be produced before court and sent to judicial custody," it says. Samuel has defended the video in which he flagged Harish's lack of credentials saying he was acting in the consumer interest. In a statement on X, Samuel said he was "deeply saddened, heavily grieving, shocked and frozen at what has happened and I mourn the loss of life". He however, rejected allegations of "cyber-bullying" Harish. "I have not cyber-bullied him. I pointed out his lack of licence and authority, misrepresentation of licence and fraud... his illegal activity. "I literally asked him in the video to come back and do this with a proper Sebi licence. I never intended or expected this drastic measure to happen and I mourn the loss," he wrote. If you're having thoughts of suicide, or know someone that might be, you can find support lines in India via the AASRA website , external or globally via Befrienders Worldwide , external . In the UK you can call the Samaritans Helpline on 116 123 or visit samaritans.org , external .
